runtimeProbeNote: All 14 tracks probed against the compiled runtime (guidance-packet-registry, packet-route-resolver, job-contract, briefcase, payment-adapter). Every track returned sellable=false, creditConsumable=false, rendererKind=none, render spec null, checkout refused, paymentAllowed=false, status=guidance_saved, resultCode=guidance_only, packetStatus=not_started, amountCents=null, and reopening returned the same terminal treatment. mt_mmrta_serving resolves routeKind=component_deferral rather than exact_supported_deferral because a pre-existing component-deferral record for that track has resolver priority; that path is closed on identical terms (no sale, no credit, no renderer) and the Briefcase still preserves this terminal treatment, so it is not a defect.

dispositions.note: Destination exact (court of conviction; AOCCRSA3F-010122 application and AOCCRSA4F-010122 order via the Arizona Judicial Branch Self-Service Center). Every fact traces to the brief: the 13-905(K) two-year and five-year waits by felony class, the 13-905(L) one-certificate rule with same-conduct grouping, the 13-905(M) Title 32 effect and 12-558.03 employer and housing-provider protections, the not-a-recommendation statement, and victim notice by the attorney for the state. The next action is superior to a bare form fetch: where the conviction is not yet set aside it routes the participant to request the certificate on the set-aside application itself, which is the brief's own scope restriction. Spanish is idiomatic and independent ('dejar sin efecto la condena', 'tarjeta de autorización con huellas dactilares').

Correct mechanism and family: Prop 207 / A.R.S. 36-2862 in the municipal or justice court that concluded the case, with the court-level form rule stated as the operative hazard. Supported facts only: the 12 July 2021 conduct line, one petition per case number, the 10-day transmission to the prosecuting agency, the 36-2862(B)(3) and Rule 36(d)(3) clear-and-convincing standard, the DPS record-correction fee for a successful non-indigent petitioner, no automatic voter re-registration, no refund of paid fines, perjury signature without notarisation. doNot correctly warns against guessing quantity, plant count or paraphernalia character, which is the brief's exact scope restriction. Spanish is a real translation, not a gloss.

Properly differentiated from the limited-jurisdiction sibling: AOC-CREM3F-071221, venue fixed by where the case ended including a justice-court case that moved up, and the superior-court-only restoration of civil rights including firearm rights, all carried by the brief. Shared language with the sibling track is confined to the same statutory scheme, so it is not boilerplate across differing mechanisms. Immigration caution matches the brief's stop condition.

The stop reason is the strongest kind available: it names the participant-side cause (offence-class mapping and the 13-911(O) exclusion screen decide the branch and the form) rather than blaming paperwork, and still gives forms AOCCRSL1F-050825 and AOCCRSL2F-050825 and the court of conviction. All ten-, five-, three- and two-year waits, the 13-911(F) stacking rule, the 13-911(G) pay-in-full-at-filing rule held distinct from the clock, the eleven 13-911(I)(5) carve-outs including fingerprint clearance cards, the Rule 36.1(b) and 13-911(L) three-year bar, and the 13-911(N) pending-charge restriction are all in the brief. Correctly keeps the money rule separate from the waiting period, which is the exact error the brief warns about.

Venue is the whole risk on this branch and the treatment treats it as such: the court where the charging document was filed, with the justice-court-complaint-followed-by-information rule sending it to superior court, and an instruction to read that off the disposition or initial-appearance record rather than the courthouse the participant remembers. Affirmatively tells the participant that no waiting period and no money condition apply here and not to let anyone say otherwise, which is a real protection and is supported by the brief's empty waitingPeriods and mechanism.

Two-stage mechanism identified exactly (FDLE Certificate of Eligibility, then the Rule 3.692 petition on Rule 3.989 forms in the circuit or county court of the circuit of arrest) with the FDLE seal-and-expunge URL from the brief. The once-per-lifetime gate is made the first action rather than a footnote, which is the brief's own hard-gate scope restriction and the highest-stakes fact on the route. Nothing required is described as optional: certified dispositions, fingerprints, the State Attorney or Statewide Prosecutor certified statement and the certificate are all carried as required, and the do-not-file-before-the-certificate instruction is explicit. Discretionary denial, the nine 943.0585(6)(b) exceptions, the 943.0584 list and Chapter 2026-114 effective 1 July 2026 all trace to the brief.

Destination exact (clerk of the district court in the county of arrest, with the free Judicial Council conviction-or-diversion form set URL) and the stop reason honestly gives both causes, including the non-commercial licence the brief records. Fulfilment-of-terms as the only clock, the three- and five-year lanes, the absence of any second-or-subsequent-DUI lane, the $176 docket fee plus non-judicial personnel charge, the KORA freeze on the whole record with the 22-4908 exception, State v. Anderson, the twelve 21-6614(i)(2) disclosure carve-outs, and the clerk-owned Certificate of Service and Mailing are all in the brief. Rule 6 is handled unusually well: the participant is told not to sign the clerk's certificate, not to write in hearing details, and not to draft the judge's findings or paragraph 8 of the denial order. The 21-6614(e) excluded-offence catalogue is not reproduced, but the treatment never asserts eligibility and routes disputed offence classification to counsel, so this is a depth point rather than a defect.

Correctly separates this arrest-only mechanism from its neighbours and names both off-ramps the brief carries: a conviction or completed diversion goes to K.S.A. 21-6614 under State v. Yrigolla, and a city-ordinance arrest to K.S.A. 12-4516a in municipal court. The fee treatment is a genuine participant protection: it states the statutory no-fee-at-all rule for identity-theft, no-probable-cause, not-guilty and dismissed-charge petitioners, tells the participant to ask the clerk before paying the $176, and does not overstate it. Critically, it identifies the mandatory 22-2410(a)(2) category as the prosecutor's or judicial officer's petition rather than the participant's, and says LegalEase does not file it. No waiting period and the on-filing separation of the court file are both from the brief.

The stop reason is track-specific and correct: the 16-12-113(2) public-safety override is unique to the currently-serving posture, that argument is never authored for a participant, resentencing computation under (3) and (4) is legal work, and custody status alone is an attorney handoff. Destination is exact at both stages, including the full DOJ CRISS Expungement postal address, phone and email from the brief. The second unit is the strongest element here: it tells the participant that under 46-18-1110(2)(b) they, not the court or clerk, must send the order with fingerprints and the DOJ form, so a Montana case that stops at the signed order leaves the conviction on the background check. Montana's expungement / sealing / removal / redesignation vocabulary is kept apart as the brief requires, one form set per conviction is stated, and the treatment correctly declines to say the conviction may be denied after expungement because no such Montana provision was located.

Mechanism correctly framed as operating on licensing consequences rather than the record, with RCW 9.94A.030(11) noted so the participant knows an issued certificate is itself visible to a sentencing court. The exemption catalogue is reproduced in full and the participant is told to check their target licence before spending anything, which is the brief's own stop condition and the point on which this route most often fails a person. Venue is exact and closed under RCW 9.97.010(2), with the operative asymmetry stated: the county-of-conviction superior court may not decline under 9.97.020(8), the residence-county court may and must then dismiss without prejudice stating its reason, and there is no transfer procedure. The graduated one-year / eighteen-month / two-year / five-year scale, the three ways to satisfy the LFO element, the 9.97.010(1)(c) bars, the 9.97.020(6) notice to the prosecutor in the county of application and in any other jurisdiction that sentenced the applicant in the preceding five years, decision on the papers under (9), and clerk transmission to the WSP identification section under (10) all trace to the brief. The openly stated limitation about multi-county filing choice is correct, not a defect: it is the brief's own stop condition and the treatment still gives an exact court and next step.

RCW 9.96.060(7) family-member application identified exactly, with the mandatory outcome stated and the sentencing court named as destination. The shared opening sentence about the CrRLJ 09.0100 draft and the missing CrRLJ 09.0200 order is a pre-committed bilingual claim recorded for this exact track in data/rcap-codex/d-v5-fallback-treatments/fallback-treatments.json, and the remainder of the stop reason, the gather list and the doNot list are specific to this route. The bereavement context is respected as the brief's trauma rule requires: three gather items only (death record, conviction docket, relationship proof) and an escalation that tells the participant to share only what is needed to route the question. No waiting period is stated because the brief states none.

Vacation is correctly distinguished from expungement throughout. The three-year rule under 9.96.060(2)(g) and the clean-period rule under (2)(h) are stated with the correct later-of trigger, and the 2024 c 296 change is handled precisely as the brief demands: the clock no longer restarts when LFOs are paid off, but completion of sentence terms including financial obligations is still required. The route's real service is telling the participant not to run this discretionary route first and naming the four mandatory alternatives, which is the brief's own participant_question limitation. Exclusions, the RCW 9.41.041 firearm point and the 9.96.060(8)(c) recidivist-charging rule are all supported. Discretion is stated as a reason no outcome can be promised, never as a promise.

Both statutory paths under RCW 9.96.060(6) are set out correctly — programme completion with proof filed, or a qualifying assessment from an RCW 71.24.115, 36.28A.450 or 71.24.589 programme plus six months of substantial compliance in a written status update — with the six enumerated conviction statutes listed and the mandatory-upon-verification outcome stated. The programme documentation is correctly presented as required, not optional, since it is the entire evidentiary basis. The open question about whether the subsection (2) bars reach this standalone route is disclosed in participant language and treated as a reason to ask counsel rather than assume in either direction, which is exactly what the brief instructs and is a correct treatment of an unresolved point, not a defect.

Distinct, non-boilerplate stop reason grounded in what the court must find rather than in form quality: tribal membership at the location of the offence and the federal injunction question under United States v. Washington and Sohappy v. Smith sit outside any court file. Correctly states that this route reaches felonies as well as misdemeanours notwithstanding RCW 9.94A.640, that the sentencing court may therefore be a superior court, that the offence date must precede 1 January 1975, and that a family member or an official tribal representative may apply where the subject has died. The destination is exact and the first call is to the tribe and to tribal legal services, which is the brief's scope restriction rather than a generic referral; the participant is told not to assert membership or treaty-rights-at-location without the tribe's written confirmation.

observationsNotDefects: Spanish naming of the Briefcase surface is not uniform across this shard: fl-expunction, ks-21-6614-diversion, ks-22-2410-arrest and mt_mmrta_serving use 'Portafolio' while wa_vac_homicide_victim_prostitution, wa_vac_misdemeanor_ordinary and wa_vac_substance_use_disorder use 'Maletin'. Both are genuine Spanish, neither is an English carry-over or a machine gloss, and no participant sees two tracks at once, so this is a product-terminology consistency item for a later pass rather than a bilingual defect.

ks-21-6614-diversion does not reproduce the K.S.A. 21-6614(e) excluded-offence catalogue. It never asserts that the participant is eligible, tells them to work out their lane and check whether it has run, and routes disputed offence classification or severity level to a lawyer who practises in that district court, so no participant is misled; adding the catalogue would be an improvement, not a correction.

mt_mmrta_serving resolves through the pre-existing component-deferral record rather than the terminal-treatment branch of the resolver. Both branches are equally closed and the Briefcase preserves the terminal treatment on reopen, and the component-deferral participant text ('MMRTA Form A is not included') does not contradict this treatment.
reviewStandardNotes: Every participant-facing string in all 14 tracks carries both en and es, no es string is identical to its en counterpart, and no en/es list differs in length.

No prohibited participant phrase from the schema appears in either language in any track, and no generic referral ('contact a lawyer', 'your local court', 'see your state's website') appears as a destination.

Every track's runtimeContract matches the schema exactly: sellable false, paymentAllowed false, checkoutSuppressed true, renderJobAllowed false, rendererKind none, packetPlan null, packetPromise none, packet and partner credit consumption none, resultCode guidance_only, packetStatus not_started, paymentStatus not_applicable, status guidance_saved; reviewState pending_independent_review, candidateOnly true, promotionEffect none, ledgerEffect none.

Long shared strings across tracks were enumerated and every one sits between sibling tracks in the same statutory family (the two AZ marijuana courts, the two AZ 13-911 branches, the WA vacation family) and restates an instruction the brief carries for each of those tracks individually, so no boilerplate spans genuinely differing mechanisms.

The sentence shared by three WA tracks about the CrRLJ 09.0100 draft and the missing CrRLJ 09.0200 proposed order was traced to data/rcap-codex/d-v5-fallback-treatments/fallback-treatments.json, which carries it as a pre-committed bilingual claim keyed to each of those three track ids.

Every deadline, fee, waiting period, address, form number, consent requirement and eligibility rule asserted in these 14 treatments was checked against that track's brief. No unsupported fact was found.
